Prompt-injection results (4 attempts, all answered exactly) describe one model on one date and are not a proof of resistance
Protects bids from the operator, not from the model TEE; says nothing about a hardware-isolated Roost of our own (GAP-004 stays open)
Needs NEARAI_API_KEY; offline suite (verification 10) uses a mock gateway
Verified on the working tree before commit

claim: A charged round leaves out bidders who cannot cover their exact worst-case charge, using escrow read from the contract at one block that two or more providers each vouch for, and fails closed when the chain cannot be read; on testnet a settlement that charged an unfunded member was rejected by the contract, and after the signed round was abandoned the reader left that member out and the settlement landed. This makes a rejected round much rarer, not impossible: a member whose exit timer has run can still leave between the read and the payout
limitations: The first live run (docs/lab-runs/20261108T103619Z-433a) used a local host; the hosted Roost on real TDX hardware is covered by CLM-ROOST-HOSTED-03
The race itself (a member leaving between the read and the payout) was not tested live; raceFree is an estimate and was false in the live run
Two providers agreeing on one block is not proof that they are honest or independent
One operator controlled every account in the run
An abandoned round's signature stays valid on chain; the record of it is in memory and lost on restart
Two-room settlements need a pinned block; that path is unit-tested, not run live
The check covers inability to pay; a member who deposits then exits is the race above
